sections.name: File setup, id, depth
sections.title: Shared building blocks
sections.what: Defines the rule for IDs (1 to 64 characters) and the three depth levels: quick, tactical and analyst.
sections.why: Likely reason: shared rules mean each event rule is written once.

sections.name: EVENT_SCHEMAS, EventName, EventProps, CLIENT_EVENTS, clientEventInput
sections.title: Event rules and browser list
sections.what: Lists every tracked event with the only details it may carry. Also lists the events a browser may send. Four events, including locked calls and reveals, are server only, so a browser cannot fake them.
sections.why: Likely reason: the KPI figures depend on those four events being trustworthy.
sections.watch_out: A new event must be added here, and a browser event must also go in the browser list, or the event is refused.

summary: Lists every tracked event and the only details each event may carry.
why: Likely reason: one list keeps the server, the browser and the KPI calculations in agreement.
how: 1. Define the shared rules for IDs and depth levels. 2. Write one rule per event. 3. Build the list of event names and types. 4. List which events a browser may send, and parse that input.
inputs: None directly. Other modules read these rules.
outputs: The event rules, event names, the list of browser events, and a parser for browser input.
risks: Changing a rule can cause events the app already sends to be refused.
debug: If an event is refused, check its name against the list and its details against its rule.
